title: HTTP Status Code
body:
A three-digit number in the response line telling the client how the request went. Every status code is generated on the **server**, even the 4xx ones that describe a mistake the client made.

| Range | Meaning | Common examples |
|---|---|---|
| 1xx | Informational | 100 Continue |
| 2xx | Success | 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content |
| 3xx | Redirect | 301 Moved Permanently, 302 Found, 304 Not Modified |
| 4xx | Client made a mistake | 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 429 Too Many Requests |
| 5xx | Server made a mistake | 500 Internal Server Error, 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable |

Two distinctions worth memorising. **401 vs 403**: 401 means the server could not verify who you are at all (missing or invalid credentials — really an [[Authentication]] failure); 403 means it verified exactly who you are and that identity is still not allowed ([[Authorization]] failure). **502 vs 500**: 500 means the app itself threw; 502 Bad Gateway means their [[Load Balancer]] got a bad response from their own app server behind it. 304 Not Modified is part of [[HTTP Caching]], and 429 is [[Rate Limiting]].
